title: Indian-Origin Lakshmanan Meyyappan Holds Guinness Record as World's Youngest Chartered Accountant
excerpt: Meyyappan earned his ACCA qualification at 16 years and 170 days during the COVID-19 pandemic, and now works as a Senior Research Analyst at Century Financial in Dubai while pursuing an MSc in Finance.
body:
• Lakshmanan Meyyappan, born in India on January 11, 2005, qualified as a chartered accountant at 16 years and 170 days on June 30, 2021
  • Guinness World Records formally recognized the achievement in February 2026
  • He completed the ACCA qualification in approximately one year, starting at age 15 during the COVID-19 lockdowns
  • Now based in Dubai, he serves as Senior Research Analyst at Century Financial and has also earned the CFA charter

Lakshmanan Meyyappan, an Indian-origin finance professional based in Dubai, holds the Guinness World Record for the youngest chartered accountant — a title he earned at 16 years and 170 days when he qualified on June 30, 2021. Guinness World Records formally recognized the achievement in February 2026, confirmed by the organization's official records.

A Pandemic-Era Achievement

Meyyappan began pursuing the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) qualification shortly after completing his 10th board examinations. Starting at 15, he completed the entire program in approximately one year — a timeline that coincided with the COVID-19 pandemic, when lockdowns created uninterrupted study time that he used to accelerate through the syllabus.

https://x.com/NewsX/status/2089315324994920457

The ACCA qualification, recognized in over 180 countries, typically takes candidates two to three years to complete. Meyyappan's compressed timeline reflects what Century Financial, his current employer, described as "exceptional individual discipline" and "a highly focused and accelerated learning journey."

"This milestone means a lot to me, but I have never approached qualifications as a race. What mattered was understanding how finance works in the real world and building skills that remain relevant over time. When learning is driven by curiosity rather than speed, the outcome is far more meaningful."

— Lakshmanan Meyyappan

From Record-Breaker to Research Analyst

After achieving the ACCA qualification, Meyyappan did not slow down. He went on to earn the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charter — one of the most demanding credentials in investment management, with a typical pass rate below 50% for each of its three levels. He is currently pursuing a Master of Science in Finance.

At Century Financial, a UAE-based investment firm with over 35 years of presence in the region, Meyyappan works as a Senior Research Analyst. His responsibilities span investments, research and analysis, and strategic decision-making across financial markets. Outside work, he designs and builds watches — a hobby he maintains alongside his professional career.

A Record With Indian Roots

India has a long history of producing young chartered accountants. The previous Guinness record for the youngest male CA was held by Ramendra Chandra Ganguli of Lucknow, who achieved the distinction at age 19 in May 1956. Nandini Agrawal from Madhya Pradesh holds the record for the youngest female CA, qualifying at 19 years and 330 days in 2021. Nischal Narayanam, a child prodigy from Hyderabad known for multiple Guinness memory records, became India's youngest CA at 19.

Meyyappan's achievement at 16 represents a generational leap in what was already a competitive field for Indian and Indian-origin candidates. The record underscores the growing role of internationally portable qualifications like ACCA and CFA in enabling young Indians to build global finance careers from an early age.

What's Next

Meyyappan continues to build his career in Dubai's financial sector while completing his MSc. His trajectory — from pandemic-era studying to a Guinness record to a professional research role — illustrates the kind of accelerated career path that international qualifications can enable for Indian-origin professionals in the Gulf and beyond.
